key_insight: Encoder–decoder operator learning can be analyzed in a resolution-independent way by passing to a limiting kernel, which cleanly separates encoding effects, optimization error, and regularization error.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical recipe for designing and scaling operator-learning models across discretizations, with guarantees for kernel methods and wide encoder–decoder neural networks when input/output resolutions change.
method: Construct an operator-valued kernel on the original function spaces from a matrix-valued kernel on the encoded space.
Prove convergence of the induced kernels to a limiting kernel via operator-norm convergence of their integral operators.
Derive SGD and NTK generalization/error bounds that isolate encoding-induced terms, optimization decay, and finite-width effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports upper and lower error bounds, plus polynomial parameter and sample complexity guarantees, for regularized SGD and wide encoder–decoder networks under algebraically decaying encoding errors.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on asymptotic resolution growth and kernel/NTK assumptions, so finite-resolution implementations may still see non-negligible encoding error or width effects.
paper_title: Resolution-Independent Analysis of Encoder--Decoder Operator Learning via Limiting Kernels
